The '''2011 Canadian federal election''' was held on May 2, 2011, to elect members to the [[House of Commons of Canada|House of Commons]] of the [[41st Canadian Parliament]].

The [[writs of election]] for the 2011 election were issued by [[Governor General of Canada|Governor General]] [[David Johnston (governor general)|David Johnston]] on March 26. [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Stephen Harper]] advised the Governor General to dissolve parliament after the House of Commons passed a [[motion of non-confidence]] against the government, finding it to be in [[contempt of Parliament]]. A few days before, the three opposition parties had rejected the [[Federal minority governments in Canada|minority government]]'s proposed budget.<ref name="macleans1">{{cite web |last=Wells |first=Paul |url=http://www.macleans.ca/2011/05/05/not-feeling-the-love/ |title=The untold story of the 2011 election: Chapter 2 |publisher=[[Maclean's]] |date=2011-05-05 |access-date=2012-03-19 |archive-date=2012-04-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120423195236/http://www2.macleans.ca/2011/05/05/not-feeling-the-love/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] remained in power, increasing its seat count from a minority to a [[majority government]], marking the first election since [[1988 Canadian federal election|1988]] that a [[centre-right politics|right-of-centre]] party formed a majority government. The [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]], sometimes dubbed the "[[natural governing party]]", was reduced to third party status for the first time as they won the fewest seats in its history, and party leader [[Michael Ignatieff]] was defeated in [[Etobicoke—Lakeshore (federal electoral district)|his riding]]. The [[Bloc Québécois]] lost [[official party status]] for the first time since contesting general elections in 1993. Party leader [[Gilles Duceppe]] was defeated in [[Laurier—Sainte-Marie|his riding]] and subsequently resigned as leader. The [[New Democratic Party (Canada)|New Democratic Party]] led by [[Jack Layton]] won the largest number of seats in its history, enabling it to form the [[Official Opposition (Canada)|Official Opposition]] for the first time in the party's history, as they made a major breakthrough in [[Quebec]], though they still trailed the Conservative Party by almost ten points. The [[Green Party of Canada|Green Party]] elected its first member to the House of Commons with its leader, [[Elizabeth May]], becoming MP for [[Saanich—Gulf Islands]].

To date, this is the only election in Canadian history in which the modern day [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] won a majority of seats and one of only two times that any party achieved a majority of seats in an election since the modern Conservative Party's founding in 2003 (the other time being the Liberal Party in the [[2015 Canadian federal election|2015 election]]).

==Background==
{{main|40th Canadian Parliament}}
The [[2008 Canadian federal election|2008 federal election]] resulted in the continuation of the incumbent [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] minority government, headed by [[Stephen Harper]]. The 40th Parliament was marked by two controversial [[prorogation in Canada|prorogations]]: the first in December 2008 which ended an [[2008–2009 Canadian parliamentary dispute|attempted opposition coalition]], and the second a year following, which prompted [[2010 Canada anti-prorogation protests|public protests]]. Following the first prorogation, Michael Ignatieff and the Liberal Party provided support for the government of Prime Minister [[Stephen Harper]]. On August 31, 2009, the Liberals withdrew their backing but the NDP under [[Jack Layton]] abstained and the Conservatives survived the confidence motion.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ca.reuters.com/article/domesticNews/idCATRE58T4BE20091001 |first=David |last=Ljunggren |title=Canada's government survives non-confidence motion |website=[[Reuters]] Canada |date=2009-10-01 |access-date=2019-11-29 |archive-date=2019-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813185821/https://ca.reuters.com/article/domesticNews/idCATRE58T4BE20091001 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
Ignatieff's attempt to force a September 2009 election was reported as a miscalculation, as polls showed that most Canadians did not want another election.<ref>{{cite web|title=Despite Election Rhetoric, Seven in Ten (68%) Canadians Say There's 'No Need for an Election', Majority (51%) Says County Heading in 'Right Direction', Minority (41%) 'Wrong', Ipsos|url=http://www.ipsos-na.com/news-polls/pressrelease.aspx?id=4420|publisher=Ipsos Market Research|access-date=2011-12-18|date=2009-06-06|archive-date=2011-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111215065705/http://ipsos-na.com/news-polls/pressrelease.aspx?id=4420|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Time to make minority work|url=https://www.thestar.com/opinion/editorials/article/696242|work=The Star|access-date=2011-12-17|date=2009-09-16|archive-date=2009-09-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090924005827/http://thestar.com/opinion/editorials/article/696242|url-status=live}}</ref> Ignatieff's popularity as well as that of the Liberals dropped off considerably immediately afterwards.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/story.html?id=2221709 |title=Ignatieff closing in on Dion territory |work=[[National Post]] |date=2009-11-14}}{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

In 2011, [[Elections Canada]] laid [[In and Out scandal|charges against the Conservative Party]], alleging contraventions of the Canada Elections Act five years earlier.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=abo&dir=com/stat&document=index&lang=e |title=''Canada Elections Act'' Charges Laid |publisher=[[Elections Canada]] |access-date=2011-04-27 |date=2011-02-25 |archive-date=2019-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611213606/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=abo&dir=com%2Fstat&document=index&lang=e |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Akin |first=David |url=https://lfpress.com/news/canada/2011/02/24/17401196.html |title=PM shrugs off charges against Tories |publisher=Lfpress.com |date=2011-02-25 |access-date=2011-04-17 |archive-date=2011-02-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110227152323/http://www.lfpress.com/news/canada/2011/02/24/17401196.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=illegal>{{cite news |first=Bruce |last=Cheadle |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/tory-election-allegations-illegal-not-administrative-prosecutor-says/article1924161/ |title=Tory election allegations 'illegal' not administrative, prosecutor says |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |location=Canada |date=2011-02-28 |access-date=2011-04-17 |archive-date=2011-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110304223220/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/tory-election-allegations-illegal-not-administrative-prosecutor-says/article1924161/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This issue, along with the Bloc Québécois announcing its intention to vote against the budget, unless it contained numerous changes including $2 billion in compensation to Quebec for harmonizing PST and GST and funding for a new NHL arena in [[Quebec City]], increased the speculation that there would be an election called soon as the Conservatives rejected the Bloc demands as "blackmail".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.macleans.ca/2011/01/12/bloc-threatens-to-vote-against-budget/ |title=Bloc threatens to vote against budget |publisher=[[Maclean's]] |date=2011-01-12 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-01-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110122095833/http://www2.macleans.ca/2011/01/12/bloc-threatens-to-vote-against-budget/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 9, 2011, [[Speaker of the House of Commons of Canada|Speaker]] of the House of Commons [[Peter Milliken]] ruled that [[Bev Oda]], a [[minister of the Crown]], and, separately, the [[Cabinet of Canada|Cabinet]] itself could both possibly be in [[contempt of parliament]],<ref>{{cite news |title=PM on rulings: 'win some, lose some' |first=Laura |last=Payton |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pm-on-rulings-win-some-lose-some-1.1033320 |newspaper=[[CBC News]] |date=2011-03-09 |access-date=2011-03-26 |archive-date=2013-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323212231/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/story/2011/03/09/pol-speaker-rulings.html |url-status=live}}</ref> the latter for its ongoing refusal to meet opposition requests for details of proposed bills and their cost estimates.<ref name=findings>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mps-report-finds-government-in-contempt-1.1091382 |title=MPs' report finds government in contempt |date=2011-03-21 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |access-date=2011-03-24 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110324122405/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/story/2011/03/21/pol-privilege-contempt.html |archive-date=2011-03-24}}</ref> Milliken directed both matters to committee and set as the deadline for its report March 21, 2011, one day before the budget was to be tabled. The committee found the government to be in contempt of Parliament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.parl.gc.ca/content/hoc/Committee/403/PROC/Reports/RP5047570/procrp27/procrp27-e.pdf |title=Question of Privilege Relating to the Failure of the Government To Fully Provide the Documents as Ordered by the House: Report of the Standing Committee on Procedure and House Affairs |access-date=2011-04-26 vote divided along party lines, with the governing but minority Conservative [[Member of Parliament (Canada)|members of Parliament]] (MPs) opposing the finding and issuing a dissenting report.<ref ==Campaign slogans==
<!-- Let's try to keep this section in alphabetical order by party, please. -->
The parties' [[political slogan|campaign slogans]] for the 2011 election:{{citation needed|date = May 2014}}
* Bloc Québécois: "{{lang|fr|Parlons Québec|italic=unset}}" (Let's talk about Quebec)
* Conservative Party: "Here For Canada / {{lang|fr|Ici pour le Canada|italic=unset}}". In francophone Quebec, Harper ran under the slogan "Notre région au pouvoir" (Our Region in Power).<ref name="quebecslogan">{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/inside-politics-blog/2011/04/here-for-canada-except-in-quebec.html |title=Here in Canada except in Quebec |work=CBC News |location=Canada |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-08 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110412015840/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/inside-politics-blog/2011/04/here-for-canada-except-in-quebec.html |archive-date=2011-04-12 |last1=Fitz-Morris |first1=James}}</ref>
* Green Party: "It's Time" & "Canada needs Elizabeth May but only you can elect her"
* Liberal Party: "Rise Up Canada" & "Change we need, from a proven team." The first one refers to Harper's contempt charge. The second one was used after the NDP's surge in the opinion polls, making reference to the fact that it has never formed a federal government.
* New Democratic Party: "Working For Families / {{lang|fr|Travaillons ensemble|italic=unset}}", "You have a choice", and "That's Canadian Leadership"

|Long gun registry||Harper pledged to scrap the [[long-gun]] [[Canadian Firearms Registry|registry]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Joe Friesen and John Ibbitson|title=Harper courts rural ridings with vow to kill gun registry|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/harper-courts-rural-ridings-with-vow-to-kill-gun-registry/article1970912/?from=sec368|access-date=2011-04-04|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-04-04|archive-date=2011-04-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110408070000/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/harper-courts-rural-ridings-with-vow-to-kill-gun-registry/article1970912/?from=sec368|url-status=dead}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|Crime strategies||The Conservative platform included a promise to consolidate twelve crime bills into at least one omnibus bill and pass it within 100&nbsp;days of forming a majority government. The bills included within that list would crack down on organized drug crime, end house arrest for violent criminals and establish tougher sentences and mandatory jail time for sexual offences against children.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/conservative-platform-harper-pledges-to-slash-4-billion-in-spending |title=Conservative platform: Harper pledges to slash $4-billion in spending |work=[[National Post]] |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-26 |archive-date=2021-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185725/https://nationalpost.com/category/news/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The opposition parties claimed the crime bills were not costed fully, and the opposition parties countered that this would create a US style system of prisons.<ref name=transcript>{{cite news |url=http://www.globalnews.ca/decisioncanada/debate/index.html |title=INTERACTIVE: Federal Election Leaders' Debate 2011 |publisher=[[Global News]] |date=2011-04-13 |access-date=2011-05-01 |archive-date=2011-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110417050907/http://www.globalnews.ca/decisioncanada/debate/index.html |url-status=live}}</ref> The Conservatives have not released the costs for expanding the [[prison system]]. The other parties state that more focus should be given on [[crime prevention]], so that it doesn't happen in the first place.<ref name=transcript/> The New Democratic Party (NDP) stated that their promise to hire 2,500 more [[police officers]] to patrol the streets, will help in preventing crime from occurring in the first place.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/unveils+plan+stamp+gang+violence+during+Surrey+stop/4580143/story.html |title=NDP unveils plan to stamp out gang violence during Surrey stop |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-18}}{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Gloria |last=Galloway |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ndp-pledge-aims-to-stamp-out-gang-related-crime-at-its-source/article1974770/ |title=NDP pledge aims to stamp out gang-related crime at its source |work=The Globe and Mail  |date=2011-04-07 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414112439/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ndp-pledge-aims-to-stamp-out-gang-related-crime-at-its-source/article1974770/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cknw.com/Channels/Reg/NewsLocal/Story.aspx?ID=1398353 |title=Layton vows crime crackdown |publisher=Cknw.com |date=2011-04-07 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926233144/http://www.cknw.com/Channels/Reg/NewsLocal/Story.aspx?ID=1398353 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/07/17905161.html |title=NDP unveils crime policy &#124; Decision 2011 &#124; News |newspaper=Toronto Sun |date=2011-04-07 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2012-10-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002172806/http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/07/17905161.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|colspan ="2"|Defence policy||The Conservatives plan to purchase 65 [[Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II Canadian procurement|F-35 Lightning II]] jet fighters. Stating that "Our [[defence policy]] is broken", the NDP announced that they would prioritize investment in [[naval ships]] over new fighter jets. The NDP stated that this would be a good opportunity to keep [[shipbuilding]] expertise and jobs in Canada.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ndp-prioritizes-ships-over-jets-1.1074350 | work=CBC News | title=NDP prioritizes ships over jets | date=2011-04-08 | access-date=2011-04-10 | archive-date=2011-04-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409171415/http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/nova-scotia/story/2011/04/08/cv-election-ndp-esquimalt.html | url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/08/17922626.html |title=New ships not jets, say NDP &#124; Decision 2011 &#124; News |newspaper=Toronto Sun |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409161430/http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/08/17922626.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Gloria |last=Galloway |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/layton-pans-tory-defence-plan-unveils-made-in-canada-alternative/article1976679/?from=sec368 |title=Layton pans Tory defence plan, unveils made-in-Canada alternative |work=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2012-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025011110/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/layton-pans-tory-defence-plan-unveils-made-in-canada-alternative/article1976679/?from=sec368 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Murray |last=Brewster |author-link=Murray Brewster |url=http://www.globalregina.com/says+replacing+navy+aging+supply+ships+would+defence+priority/4586012/story.html |title=NDP says replacing navy's aging supply ships would be its defence priority |publisher=[[Global News]] |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2012-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314220700/http://www.globalregina.com/says+replacing+navy+aging+supply+ships+would+defence+priority/4586012/story.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

|rowspan = "5"|Economy and fiscal policy||Balanced budget and recession||Conservatives argued that they steered the economy through the [[2008 financial crisis]], and promised to eliminate the [[budget deficit]] by 2014–15.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/politics/Tories+kill+deficit+early/4582506/story.html |title=Tories vow to kill deficit early |work=National Post  |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-18}}{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/tories-vow-to-eliminate-deficit-early-1.1000691 | work=CBC News | title=Tories vow to eliminate deficit early | date=2011-04-08 | access-date=2011-04-14 | archive-date=2011-04-11 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110411105923/http://www.cbc.ca/news/business/story/2011/04/08/cv-election-day14.html | url-status=live}}</ref> Former Prime Minister Paul Martin, campaigning for the Liberals, challenged assertions, noting  that his Liberal government left a $13&nbsp;billion [[budget surplus]], before the Conservatives took power.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.saultstar.com/ArticleDisplay.aspx?e=3035065 |title=If this election's about the economy, let's hope the parties aren't stupid |publisher=The Sault Star |last1=Mills |first1=Tom |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720204142/http://www.saultstar.com/ArticleDisplay.aspx?e=3035065 |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=martin1>{{cite news |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/16/18015056.html |title=Paul Martin rips Tory fiscal record |last1=Dormer |first1=Dave |agency=QMI |newspaper=Toronto |url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 2010, Paul Martin had been invited to the prestigious Global ARC conference to discuss that elimination of the Canadian government deficit.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.investmentreview.com/news/europe-can-learn-from-canada-john-major-paul-martin-4345 |title=Europe Can Learn From Canada: John Major, Paul Martin |publisher=Investmentreview.com when he was Finance minister working under Jean Chretien, his blocking of [[Big Five (banks)#Proposed mergers|proposed bank mergers]] is what actually sheltered Canada from the worst effects of the |url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20110410/ap_on_re_ca/cn_harper_s_canada_remake |title=Prime minister nudging Canada to the right – Associated Press |first=Rob |last=Gilles |work=news.yahoo.com as claimed.<ref name=Sciencefiction/>
|- valign="top"
|Corporate tax cuts and job creation strategy||The Conservatives stated that their plan to cut corporate taxes from 16.5% to 15%, will create more jobs.<ref>{{cite news|last=Taber|first=Jane|title=Ignatieff heads to Vancouver pharmacy to unveil another platform plank|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ignatieff-heads-to-vancouver-pharmacy-to-unveil-another-platform-plank/article1962922/|access-date=2011-03-30|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-30|archive-date=2011-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401131253/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ignatieff-heads-to-vancouver-pharmacy-to-unveil-another-platform-plank/article1962922/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Harper stated that an increase in corporate taxes will create job losses across Canada. Layton countered by saying currently the jobs are shipped overseas, and pledged a $4,500 job creation tax credit to all businesses per new hire.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/03/30/17804416.html |title=Layton announces job creation measures |newspaper=Toronto Sun |date=2011-03-30 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110407184305/http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/03/30/17804416.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Layton further went to say that [[small business]] are the ones creating more jobs, thus he promised to lower the tax rate for small business from 11% to 9%. He then went on to say the big business are using the corporate tax cuts by providing their CEOs with big bonuses, and thus pledged to increase their tax rate to 19.5%.<ref name=transcript/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://money.canoe.com/money/business/canada/archives/2011/03/20110330-143448.html |title=NDP's small biz measures a double-edged sword |publisher=canoe.com |date=2011-03-30 |last1=Singleton |first1=Sharon |access-date=2011-04-18}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The Liberals on the other hand, will raise the rate to 18%, stating that it will be competitive but not excessively low.
|- valign="top"
|Increasing Canada Pension Plan||The NDP promised a gradual doubling of [[Canada Pension Plan]] and QPP benefits, in conjunction with the provinces, with an increase in payroll deductions of as much as 2.5&nbsp;per cent.<ref name=promise>{{cite web|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/key-election-campaign-promises-so-far-from-the-federal-parties-1.626544 |title=Key election campaign promises so far from the federal parties |work=CTV News |date=2011-04-14 |access-date=2011-04-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329144355/http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20110402/key-campaign-election-promises-040102/20110414?s_name=election2011 |archive-date=2012-03-29}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|HST referendum in BC||If BC voters were to reject the [[Sales taxes in British Columbia|Harmonized Sales Tax]] in the upcoming referendum, the NDP promised to ensure that the penalties to be imposed by Ottawa on the HST agreement will be cancelled.<ref>{{cite news |last=Fowlie |first=Jonathan |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/should+keep+money+even+scrapped+Layton/4573179/story.html |title=B.C. should keep money even if HST is scrapped: Layton |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=2011-04-07 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709213813/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/should+keep+money+even+scrapped+Layton/4573179/story.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/harper-has-ignored-health-care-problems-layton-1.1110891 |work=[[CBC News]] |title=Harper has ignored health-care problems: Layton |date=2011-04-06 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409181753/http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/story/2011/04/06/cv-election-layton-seniors.html |archive-date=2011-04-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Austin |first=Ian |url=https://theprovince.com/Layton+courting+haters/4573708/story.html |title=Layton courting B.C. HST haters |publisher=Theprovince.com |date=2011-04-07 |access-date=2011-04-18}}{{Dead link|date=May 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/06/17894741.html |title=Layton feeds off HST anger in B.C. &#124; Decision 2011 &#124; News |newspaper=Toronto Sun |date=2011-04-06 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409183355/http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/06/17894741.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|Personal taxation||Conservatives promised income splitting for tax purposes for families with children to be implemented once the budget is balanced in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|last=Carrick|first=Rob|title=A wish list for all investors in this year's election|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/personal-finance/rob-carrick/a-wish-list-for-all-investors-in-this-years-election/article1960511/|access-date=2011-03-30|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-29|archive-date=2011-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110402042505/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/globe-investor/personal-finance/rob-carrick/a-wish-list-for-all-investors-in-this-years-election/article1960511/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|rowspan = "3"|Electoral reform and political honesty||Political honesty||The New Democratic Party stated that both the Conservatives and the Liberals cannot be trusted. The NDP accused the Conservatives of creating "Liberal-style [[Political corruption|scandals]]"<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chase |first1=Steven |last2=Galloway |first2=Gloria |last3=Taber |first3=Jane |title=Federal election called for May 2 |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/federal-election-called-for-may-2/article576430/ |access-date=2021-08-07 |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |date=2011-03-26 |archive-date=2021-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807193912/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/federal-election-called-for-may-2/article576430/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and accused the Liberals of flip-flopping on issues such as [[corporate tax]] cuts, and the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|Afghanistan mission]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/layton-warns-of-tory-liberal-service-cuts-1.978418 | work=CBC News | title=Layton warns of Tory, Liberal service cuts | date=2011-04-09 | access-date=2011-04-26 | archive-date=2011-04-12 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110412004227/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/09/cv-election-layton.html | url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/968602--layton-calls-ignatieff-part-of-the-problem?bn=1 | location=Toronto | work=The Star | first=Richard J. | last=Brennan | title=Layton calls Ignatieff 'part of the problem' | date=2011-04-04 | access-date=2017-08-25 | archive-date=2012-10-24 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024031412/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/968602--layton-calls-ignatieff-part-of-the-problem?bn=1 | url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Belanger|first=Joe |url=https://lfpress.com/news/london/2011/04/04/17871561.html |title=Layton slams Harper over loan dithering &#124; London &#124; News &#124; London Free Press |publisher=[[The London Free Press]] |date=2011-04-05 |access-date=2011-04-17 |archive-date=2011-04-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110410011436/http://www.lfpress.com/news/london/2011/04/04/17871561.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Throughout the election various polls had shown the political honesty issue to be low on the list of priorities for voters. Post-media conducted a survey that found health care, the economy, taxes and jobs all more important to Canadians. Further, half of voters identified Harper as the best suited to be Prime Minister followed by Layton with one third support and Ignatieff with less than twenty percent support. On the question of a hidden agenda, Ignatieff is viewed by three times more of those polled to have a hidden agenda than Harper.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/Voters+connecting+dots/4668930/story.html |title=Voters not connecting the dots |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |last1=Boswell |first1=Randy |date=2011-04-25 |access-date=2011-05-05 |archive-date=2011-04-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110430104622/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/Voters+connecting+dots/4668930/story.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|Political financing||Conservatives pledged to phase-out [[Federal political financing in Canada#Per-vote subsidy|per-vote subsidy]] over two years, with its eventual cancellation.<ref name=promise/>
|- valign="top"
|Senate||Stephen Harper promised [[Senate of Canada|Senate]] reform without changing the constitution.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/canadian-politics/harper-lends-support-to-ontario-candidates-facing-ndp-incumbents |title=Harper pledges Senate reform, but without constitutional wrangling |work=National Post |date=2010-12-22 |access-date=2011-04-26 |archive-date=2021-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185727/https://nationalpost.com/category/news/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The NDP pledged to abolish the Senate, stating it is a waste of tax revenues and a form of [[patronage]].<ref name=transcript/>
|- valign="top"
|rowspan = "3"|Promised government programs||Newfoundland hydroelectric project and Quebec's HST||Conservatives, New Democrats and Liberals promised $4.2&nbsp;billion in loan guarantees to support the [[Lower Churchill Project|Lower Churchill River power project]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Shawn McCarthy and Steven Chase|title=Harper to back Lower Churchill mega-project in bid for Newfoundland seats|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/harper-to-back-lower-churchill-mega-project-in-bid-for-newfoundland-seats/article1963954/|access-date=2011-04-02|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-30|archive-date=2011-04-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110404054819/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/harper-to-back-lower-churchill-mega-project-in-bid-for-newfoundland-seats/article1963954/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Due to outcry from Quebec over the pledge to provide loan guarantees for the Lower Churchill project, the Conservatives promise Quebec a $2.2&nbsp;billion transfer to ease the [[Quebec Sales Tax]] to [[Harmonized Sales Tax]] transition.<ref>{{cite news|last=Chase|first=Steven|title=Harper pledges to settle multibillion-dollar HST feud with Quebec|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/harper-pledges-to-settle-multibillion-dollar-hst-feud-with-quebec/article1967422/|access-date=2011-04-01|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-04-01|archive-date=2011-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110407122547/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/harper-pledges-to-settle-multibillion-dollar-hst-feud-with-quebec/article1967422/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|Post-secondary education||Liberals promised a "Learning Passport" for high school students seeking post-secondary education.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.liberal.ca/newsroom/news-release/michael-ignatieff-announces-canadian-learning-passport/ |title=Michael Ignatieff announces Canadian Learning Passport |publisher=Liberal.ca |date=2011-03-29 |access-date=2011-04-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110503222627/http://www.liberal.ca/newsroom/news-release/michael-ignatieff-announces-canadian-learning-passport/ |archive-date=2011-05-03 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The NDP's plan is to reduce the tuition fees, by increasing [[transfer payments]] to the Provinces.
|- valign="top"
|Immigration Fairness Commissioner||Liberals proposed the establishment of an "Immigration Fairness Commissioner" to provide oversight on the entry of immigrants with professional qualifications (doctors, engineers, etc.), and to increase the number of family reunification visas.<ref>{{cite news|last=Taber|first=Jane|title=Ignatieff calls for immigration 'fairness commissioner'|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ignatieff-calls-for-immigration-fairness-commissioner/article1962566/|access-date=2011-03-30|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-29|archive-date=2011-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401100936/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ignatieff-calls-for-immigration-fairness-commissioner/article1962566/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|colspan = "2"|Health care||The NDP pledged to train 1,200 more doctors and 6,000 more nurses.<ref>{{cite news|last=Galloway|first=Gloria|title=NDP goes big with health-care ads, accusing Harper of neglect|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ndp-goes-big-with-health-care-ads-accusing-harper-of-neglect/article1961859/|access-date=2011-03-30|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-29|archive-date=2011-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110402071316/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/ndp-goes-big-with-health-care-ads-accusing-harper-of-neglect/article1961859/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |url=http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/06/17901376.html |title=Future of health care hinges on election: Layton &#124; Decision 2011 &#124; News |newspaper=Toronto Sun |date=2011-04-06 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110410135916/http://www.torontosun.com/news/decision2011/2011/04/06/17901376.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/layton-warns-canadians-about-harper-s-health-care-1.627964 |title=Layton warns Canadians about Harper's health care |work=CTV News |agency=The Canadian Press |date=2011-04-06 |access-date=2011-04-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329145902/http://www.ctv.ca/CTVNews/SpecialEvent7/20110406/layton-health-care-110406/ |archive-date=2012-03-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Gloria |last=Galloway |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/tories-will-let-health-care-fail-layton-warns-as-he-rolls-out-plan-in-bc/article1973270/ |title=Tories will let health care fail, Layton warns as he rolls out plan in B.C. |work=The Globe and Mail  |date=2011-04-06 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2011-04-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110411211312/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/tories-will-let-health-care-fail-layton-warns-as-he-rolls-out-plan-in-bc/article1973270/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/970078--canada-s-health-care-system-in-jeopardy-under-conservatives-layton?bn=1 | location=Toronto | work=The Star | first=Richard J. | last=Brennan | title=They may be New Democrats but old policies hurt profile | date=2011-04-06 | access-date=2017-08-25 | archive-date=2012-10-24 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024031438/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/970078--canada-s-health-care-system-in-jeopardy-under-conservatives-layton?bn=1 | url-status=live}}</ref> All parties promised to continue to increase healthcare transfers to provinces by 6% annually.
|- valign="top"
|rowspan = "2"|Government regulations||Improved internet and usage based billing||The New Democratic Party (NDP) promised a ban on all forms of [[usage based billing]] by ISPs, and enshrine [[net neutrality]] in law, which would prevent [[bandwidth throttling]]. The Liberals promised net neutrality as well as "functional separation" with regards to usage based billing as well as enshrining net neutrality in law, which would prevent [[bandwidth throttling]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberals-target-faster-rural-internet-service-1.1085926 |title=Liberals target faster rural internet service |author=[[CBC News]] |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |date=2011-04-06 |access-date=2011-04-06 |archive-date=2011-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111213194305/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/06/cv-election-lib-rural.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/extra-billing-for-internet-use-a-ripoff-ndp-1.1035293 |title=Extra billing for internet use a 'ripoff': NDP |author=[[CBC News]] |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |date=2011-01-20 |access-date=2011-04-06 |archive-date=2012-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109063916/http://www.cbc.ca/news/story/2011/01/20/consumer-internet-ndp.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Almost all of the established parties, with the exception of the Conservatives, outlined policies that they claim will improve Canadian Internet access.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/platforms-pro-internet-except-conservative-report-1.1126296 |title=Platforms pro-internet, except Conservative: report |work=[[CBC News]] |date=2011-04-28 |access-date=2011-04-29 |archive-date=2011-04-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110430074155/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/28/technology-internet-election-digital-platforms.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
|- valign="top"
|Cap on credit card interest rates||The NDP promised to cap [[credit card]] rates at five percentage points above the Bank of Canada's prime interest rate.<ref>{{cite news|last=Galloway|first=Gloria|title=Layton vows to cap credit-card rates|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/layton-vows-to-cap-credit-card-rates/article1961191/|access-date=2011-03-29|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=2011-03-29|archive-date=2011-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110402041206/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/layton-vows-to-cap-credit-card-rates/article1961191/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Election campaign==
===Controversies and gaffes===
{{main|Controversies in the Canadian federal election, 2011}}
A number of controversies took place during the election campaign.

===Leaders' debates===
{{See also|Canadian leaders' debates#2011 debates}}
The English- and French-language debates took place on April 12 and&nbsp;13 respectively.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Daniel |last1=Leblanc |first2=Simon |last2=Houpt |first3=Steve |last3=Ladurantaye |title=Broadcasters rule out one-on-one debate between Harper and Ignatieff, confirm May's exclusion |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/broadcasters-rule-out-one-on-one-debate-between-harper-and-ignatieff-confirm-mays-exclusion/article1964414/ |access-date=2011-03-31 |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-03-30 |archive-date=2011-04-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110403012704/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/broadcasters-rule-out-one-on-one-debate-between-harper-and-ignatieff-confirm-mays-exclusion/article1964414/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="CBC20110410NHL">{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/leaders-french-debate-bumped-by-nhl-playoffs-1.1061040 |title=How Canadian: NHL trumps debate |work=[[CBC News]] |last1=Fitz-Morris |first1=James |date=2011-04-10 |access-date=2011-04-13 |archive-date=2011-04-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110413053623/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/10/cv-election-debats-duceppe.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 29, the [[Consortium#Coopetition|consortium of broadcasters]] playing host to the debates (the [[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]], [[CTV Television Network|CTV]], [[Global Television Network|Global]], [[Télévision de Radio-Canada|Radio-Canada]] and [[TVA (TV network)|TVA]]) announced that it would only invite the leaders of the four recognized parties in the House of Commons, namely, the Conservative Party, the Liberal Party, the Bloc Québécois and the New Democratic (NDP). Therefore, the Green Party was [[Green Party of Canada#Exclusion from debates|excluded]], despite earning 6.8 per cent of the popular vote in the [[2008 Canadian federal election|2008 federal election]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Burgmann |first=Tamsyn |title=Green's Elizabeth May will fight broadcasters' decision to ditch her from debate |work=Winnipeg Free Press |agency=The Canadian Press |date=2011-03-29 |url=http://www.winnipegfreepress.com/business/breakingnews/greens-elizabeth-may-will-fight-broadcasters-decision-to-ditch-her-from-debate-118927234.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423092719/https://www.winnipegfreepress.com/business/breakingnews/greens-elizabeth-may-will-fight-broadcasters-decision-to-ditch-her-from-debate-118927234.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2023-04-23 |access-date=2011-03-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Debate over May diverts campaign Harper pushes lower corporate taxes, Layton would raise them, Ignatieff would add to CPP |newspaper=[[CBC News]] |date=2011-03-30 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/debate-over-may-diverts-campaign-1.1105297 |access-date=2011-03-30 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110402050359/http://www.cbc.ca/news/business/story/2011/03/30/cv-election.html |archive-date=2011-04-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Pynn |first1=Larry |last2=Minsky |first2=Amy |title=Greens' Elizabeth May, determined to enter debate, prepares legal action |newspaper=[[Vancouver Sun]] and Postmedia News |date=2011-03-30 |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/Greens+Elizabeth+determined+enter+debate+prepares+legal+action/4529114/story.html |access-date=2011-03-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401124131/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/Greens+Elizabeth+determined+enter+debate+prepares+legal+action/4529114/story.html |archive-date=2011-04-01 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Leblanc |first=Daniel |title=Elizabeth May excluded from election debates |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/elizabeth-may-excluded-from-election-debates/article1962085/ |access-date=2011-03-30 |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-03-30 |archive-date=2011-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401100846/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/elizabeth-may-excluded-from-election-debates/article1962085/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 30, Stephen Harper challenged Michael Ignatieff to a one-on-one televised debate.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Steven |last1=Chase |first2=Gloria |last2=Galloway |first3=Jane |last3=Taber |title=Harper and Ignatieff game for head-to-head debate |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/harper-and-ignatieff-game-for-head-to-head-debate/article1963435/ |access-date=2011-03-30 |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-03-30 |archive-date=2011-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110401100931/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/harper-and-ignatieff-game-for-head-to-head-debate/article1963435/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Although Ignatieff accepted the challenge, this was opposed by the other opposition parties. The idea was later rejected by the broadcast consortium and cancelled.

On April 1, comedian [[Rick Mercer]] suggested over Twitter hosting a one-on-one debate between Stephen Harper and Michael Ignatieff at Toronto's [[Massey Hall]]. He later added he would donate $50,000 to the charities of their choosing if they were willing to participate. Ignatieff immediately accepted the challenge and named the [[Alzheimer Society of Canada|Alzheimer Society]] as his charity of choice, as his mother succumbed to Alzheimer's disease in 1992. Harper did not respond to the challenge.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ignatieff accepts Rick Mercer debate offer |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ignatieff-accepts-rick-mercer-debate-offer-1.1084566 |access-date=2011-04-04 |date=2011-04-02 |agency=CBC |work=CBC News |archive-date=2011-04-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405140442/http://www.cbc.ca/news/offbeat/story/2011/04/02/mercer-ignatieff-harper-cv-election.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

In an interview with ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'' published on April 1, Troy Reeb, the [[Consortium#Coopetition|broadcast consortium]] chairman, discussed the process behind setting up the leaders' debates and the rationale for various decisions made, including the decision to exclude the Green Party's leader Elizabeth May.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ladurantaye |first=Steve |title=Why the TV consortium excluded Elizabeth May |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/why-the-tv-consortium-excluded-elizabeth-may/article1966583/ |access-date=2011-04-05 |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-04-01 |archive-date=2011-04-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405002145/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/why-the-tv-consortium-excluded-elizabeth-may/article1966583/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 5, the Federal Court rejected the Green Party's request for an expedited hearing on the matter prior to the scheduled debates.<ref>{{cite news |title=Judge denies Elizabeth May's bid to join leaders' debates |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/judge-denies-elizabeth-mays-bid-to-join-leaders-debates/article1971474/ |access-date=2011-04-05 |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=2011-04-05 |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=2011-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110408063724/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/judge-denies-elizabeth-mays-bid-to-join-leaders-debates/article1971474/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 10, the date of the French leaders debate was changed from April 14 to 13 due to worries of broadcasting conflicts with the [[2011 NHL playoffs|NHL playoffs]] scheduled for April 14.<ref name="CBC20110410NHL"/> Also on April 10, Elizabeth May participated in a panel interview on [[CHCH-TV]] in [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]], which she was invited to attend, as were the leaders of the Bloc, Liberals, New Democrats and Conservatives, by [[Channel Zero Inc.|Channel Zero]], whose president was disappointed by May's exclusion from the leaders' debates.<ref>{{cite news |title=CHCH-TV to Broadcast "Elizabeth May, For the Record" Live this Sunday, April&nbsp;10, 2011 – 8pm&nbsp;ET |url=http://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/April2011/08/c2709.html |access-date=2011-04-10 |publisher=CNW Group |date=2011-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009050509/http://www.newswire.ca/en/story/733245/chch-tv-to-broadcast-elizabeth-may-for-the-record-live-this-sunday-april-10-2011-8pm-et |archive-date=2012-10-09 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Small parties public forum===
A joint press conference and public forum was staged by 11 of the 18 registered parties and one unregistered party on April 23, 2011, at [[York University]].  Forum organizers invited the leaders from all registered political parties who do not have seats in parliament.<ref>{{cite news |first=Anna |last=Di Carlo |url=http://www.cpcml.ca/Tmld2011/D41062.htm |title=The Marxist-Leninist Daily |publisher=Cpcml.ca |date=2011-04-18 |access-date=2011-05-14 |archive-date=2011-05-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110503161615/http://cpcml.ca/Tmld2011/D41062.htm |url-status=live}}</ref> Parties were able to explain their platforms and responded to questions from the audience.  As a forum, the goal was an inter-party discussion of major issues, however some debate did occur.

Participants in the forum were the [[Animal Alliance Environment Voters Party of Canada|Animal Alliance Environmental Voters]], the [[Canadian Action Party]], the [[Christian Heritage Party of Canada|Christian Heritage Party]], the [[Communist Party of Canada|Communist Party]], the [[First Peoples National Party of Canada|First Peoples National]], the [[Libertarian Party of Canada|Libertarian Party]], the [[Marijuana Party of Canada|Marijuana Party]], the [[Communist Party of Canada (Marxist–Leninist)|Marxist–Leninist Party]], the [[Rhinoceros Party]], and the [[Pirate Party of Canada|Pirate Party]].

Green Party leader [[Elizabeth May]] refused to participate in the forum claiming they are not one of "the small, fringe parties".<ref name=fringedebate>{{cite news |title=Green Party snubs fringe debate |work=National Post |location=Canada |first=Adrian |last=Humphreys |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/canadian-politics/green-party-snubs-fringe-debate |date=2011-04-05 |access-date=2011-04-09 |archive-date=2021-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185729/https://nationalpost.com/category/news/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===New Democratic Party surge===
In the week before the leaders debate, on April 8, a poll showed the New Democratic Party (NDP) support at 13.2%.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Richard J. |last=Brennan |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/972241--ndp-fortunes-falling-fast-in-latest-poll |title=NDP fortunes falling fast in latest poll |journal=Toronto Star |date=2011-04-09 |access-date=2011-04-25 |archive-date=2012-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024031459/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/972241--ndp-fortunes-falling-fast-in-latest-poll |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Gloria |last=Galloway |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/though-chips-look-down-laytons-eager-to-ante-up-for-debates/article1978060 |title=Layton remains game despite polls showing he's the odd man out |work=The Globe and Mail  |date=2011-04-08 |access-date=2011-04-25}}</ref>
A reversal of fortune began on April 16, when an Angus Reid poll indicated a tie in support for the NDP and the Liberals, both polling at 25%.<ref>{{cite news |first=Joanna |last=Smith |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/976225 |title=NDP moves into tie with Liberals: Poll |work=Toronto Star |date=2011-04-13 |access-date=2011-04-18 |location=Toronto |archive-date=2011-05-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110501223620/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/976225 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/canada-politics-idUSN1822211320110418 |title=Canada's NDP pushes for bigger place in election sun |publisher=Reuters |date=2011-02-14 |access-date=2011-04-18 |first=Randall |last=Palmer |archive-date=2016-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104200923/http://www.reuters.com/article/canada-politics-idUSN1822211320110418 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/layton-sees-growing-quebec-support-targets-liberals-1.1076764 |title=Layton sees growing Quebec support, targets Liberals |work=CBC News |date=2011-04-18 |access-date=2011-04-18 |archive-date=2013-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130417162852/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/18/cv-election-layton-quebec-812.html |url-status=live}}</ref> The New Democrats' poll numbers then moved significantly ahead of the Liberals and slightly or moderately behind the Conservatives.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/poll-shows-ndp-liberals-in-statistical-tie-1.634836 |title=Poll shows NDP, Liberals in statistical tie |work=CTV News |date=2011-04-22 |access-date=2011-04-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426112552/http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20110422/federal-election-campaign-poll-day-28-110422/20110422?s_name=election2011 |archive-date=2011-04-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/surging-ndp-support-changes-campaign-dynamic-1.1101061 |title=Surging NDP support changes campaign dynamic |work=[[CBC News]] |date=2011-04-21 |access-date=2011-04-22 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110424072809/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/canadavotes2011/story/2011/04/21/cv-election-ndp-quebec-803.html |archive-date=2011-04-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.harrisdecima.ca/news/releases/201104/1160-conservatives-lead-five-ndp-surges-past-liberals|title=Conservatives Lead By Five; NDP Surges Past Liberals|publisher=Harris/Decima|date=2011-04-28|access-date=2011-04-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110430224105/http://www.harrisdecima.ca/news/releases/201104/1160-conservatives-lead-five-ndp-surges-past-liberals|archive-date=2011-04-30|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The surge began in Quebec, with the NDP surprising many observers by surpassing the previously front-running Bloc in Quebec. In the entirety of Canada, the NDP surged past the Liberals to take the second place behind the Conservatives; in Quebec, the NDP took first place.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/canada-us-politics-ekos-idCATRE73O5UR20110425 |title=NDP surges to strong second place in poll |publisher=Reuters |date=2011-04-25 |access-date=2011-04-25 |first=Janet |last=Guttsman |archive-date=2016-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104200922/http://www.reuters.com/article/canada-us-politics-ekos-idCATRE73O5UR20110425 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="EKOS">{{cite web|url = http://www.ekospolitics.com/wp-content/uploads/full_report_april_21_2011.pdf|title = NDP Breakout Continues As Everyone Else Spins Wheels|access-date=2011-04-23|last = [[Ekos Research Associates|EKOS]]|date = April 2011|archive-date=2020-12-04|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201204103935/https://www.ekospolitics.com/wp-content/uploads/full_report_april_21_2011.pdf|url-status = dead}}</ref> The NDP surge became the dominant narrative of the last week of the campaign, as other parties turned their attacks on the party.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/surge+dominates+talk+federal+campaign+trail/4685960/story.html |title=NDP surge dominates talk on federal campaign trail |last1=Cohen |first1=Tobi |last2=Raj |first2=Althia |last3=Kennedy |first3=Mark |work=[[Vancouver Sun]]|date=2011-04-27 |access-date=2011-04-27 |archive-date=2011-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110502043910/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/surge+dominates+talk+federal+campaign+trail/4685960/story.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Ruth Ellen Brosseau]], the NDP candidate in [[Berthier—Maskinongé]], won despite not running a campaign, barely speaking French at this time<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2011/04/28/in_frenchspeaking_riding_ndp_candidate_speaks_little_french.html |title=In French-speaking riding, NDP candidate speaks little French |first1=Chung |last1=Andrew |work=Toronto Star |date=2011-04-28 |access-date=2015-04-25 |archive-date=2016-01-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125170004/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2011/04/28/in_frenchspeaking_riding_ndp_candidate_speaks_little_french.html |url-status=live}}</ref> and being on holiday in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]] at the time of the election.<ref name=StarResultsPostElection/> The NDP's rise in popularity was nicknamed '''Orange Crush''', an allusion to [[Orange Crush|the soft drink with the same name]] and the party's colour.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/inside-politics-blog/2011/08/remembering-jack-layton.html|title=Remembering Jack Layton|publisher=[[CBC News]]|first=Laura|last=Payton|quote=The NDP's surging popularity, especially in Quebec, during the last election came to be known as the Orange Crush.|date=2011-08-22|access-date=2013-08-12|archive-date=2013-06-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130619151636/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/inside-politics-blog/2011/08/remembering-jack-layton.html|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also nicknamed the '''Orange Wave'''.<ref>{{Cite news|title=The decline and fall of the NDP in Quebec |language=en-US|work=CBC News |last1=Montpetit |first1=Jonathan |date=2019-08-26 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/ndp-new-democrat-jagmeet-singh-quebec-1.5336302|access-date=2021-01-11|archive-date=2021-07-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210651/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/ndp-new-democrat-jagmeet-singh-quebec-1.5336302|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Election spending==
Pre-campaign, there are no limits to what a political party, candidate, or third party can spend — spending rules are only in force once the writ is dropped and the campaign has officially begun.

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Spending limits for the 2011 federal election
!  !! Spending Limit !! Notes
|-
| '''Political Parties''' || $21,025,793.23 || If full slate of 308 candidates.
|-
| '''Party Candidates''' (Average electoral district) || $28,244,498.50 ($91,702.92) || If full slate of 308 candidates.  Each electoral district is subject to specific spending limits according to population and density.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=limits%2Flimitcan&lang=e |title = Final Election Expenses Limits for Candidates 43rd General Election – October 21, 2019 – Elections Canada |access-date=2021-08-07 |archive-date=2021-01-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125212631/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=limits%2Flimitcan&lang=e |url-status=live}}</ref> The limits for candidates varied from $69,635 in the electoral district of Malpeque, Prince Edward Island, to $134,352 in Oak Ridges–Markham, Ontario.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=res&dir=ces&document=part6&lang=e |title = Elections Canada Online {{!}} The Electoral System of Canada  |access-date=2015-08-02 |archive-date=2015-08-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150820005709/http://elections.ca/content.aspx?section=res&dir=ces&document=part6&lang=e |url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
| '''Third Parties''' (corporations, unions, special interest groups, etc.) || $150,000 || Election advertising expenses limit.  Of that amount, no more than $3,000 can be incurred to promote or oppose the election of one or more candidates in a particular electoral district.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=thi%2Flimits&lang=e |title = Elections Canada Online {{!}} Third Party Election Advertising Expenses Limits  |access-date=2021-08-07 |archive-date=2015-07-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150718060744/http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=thi%2Flimits&lang=e |url-status=live}}</ref>
|}

==Endorsements==
{{main|Newspaper endorsements in the Canadian federal election, 2011}}
Most major newspapers endorsed the Conservatives, and none solely endorsed the Liberals or Greens. Canada's highest circulated newspaper, the ''[[Toronto Star]]'', endorsed the NDP but also advised readers to vote against the Conservatives.
