===Overview of results===
[[File:Élection-fédérale-canadienne-2011.png|right|thumb|250px|Analysis of results by riding, together with comparisons from previous election and at dissolution.]]
[[File:Elections2011wikipedia.JPG|right|thumb|250px|Canada Federal Election 2011 by Province]]
[[File:Canada 2011 Federal Election seats.svg|thumb|right|250px|Rendition of party representation in the [[41st Canadian Parliament]] decided by this election
{{legend|#6495ED|Conservatives (166)}}
{{legend|#F4A460|New Democrats (103)}}
{{legend|#F08080|Liberals (34)}}
{{legend|#87CEFA|Bloc Québécois (4)}}
{{legend|#2F873E|Green Party (1)}}]]

With an overall voter turnout of 61.4% and 14,823,408 ballots cast,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Reilly|first=Ian|title="Amusing Ourselves to Death?" Social Media, Political Satire, and the 2011 Election|journal=Canadian Journal of Communication|year=2011|volume=36|issue=3|page=503|doi=10.22230/cjc.2011v36n3a2508|doi-access=}}</ref> the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] remained in power, moving from a [[minority government|minority]] to a [[majority government]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://enr.elections.ca/National_e.aspx |title=Preliminary Results |publisher=[[Elections Canada]] |access-date=2011-05-03 |archive-date=2012-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120228042630/http://enr.elections.ca/National_e.aspx |url-status=live}}</ref> by winning 166 of the 308 seats.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kanada: Konservative erringen Sieg|url=https://www.welt.de/print/welt_kompakt/print_politik/article13334432/Kanada-Konservative-erringen-Sieg.html|access-date=2011-05-11|newspaper=[[Die Welt]]|date=2011-05-04|lang=de|archive-date=2011-05-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110509154721/http://www.welt.de/print/welt_kompakt/print_politik/article13334432/Kanada-Konservative-erringen-Sieg.html|url-status=live}}</ref>  The [[New Democratic Party (Canada)|New Democratic Party]] won the largest number of seats in their history, including a large majority of seats in [[2011 Canadian federal election in Quebec|Quebec]] (where they had previously only ever elected two candidates<ref name=ndpqc group=fn />) and formed the [[Official Opposition (Canada)|Official Opposition]] for the first time. The [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] won the fewest seats in their history and party leader [[Michael Ignatieff]] was defeated in his own [[electoral district (Canada)|riding]].<ref name=libhist group=fn /> The [[Bloc Québécois]], which had always won at least a majority of seats in Quebec in every election of their existence, lost nearly all their seats, and thus also their [[official party status]], including the seat of their leader [[Gilles Duceppe]].<ref>{{cite news|last=LeBlanc|first=Daniel|title=Duceppe resigns as Bloc leader after losing riding|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/duceppe-resigns-as-bloc-leader-after-losing-riding/article2007598/|access-date=2011-05-11|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=2011-05-02|archive-date=2011-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110505112408/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/duceppe-resigns-as-bloc-leader-after-losing-riding/article2007598/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Green Party of Canada|Green Party]] leader [[Elizabeth May]] became the first [[Member of Parliament (Canada)|Member]] of [[Parliament of Canada|Parliament]] elected to represent the party.<ref name="StarResultsPostElection">{{cite news|last=Taylor|first=Lesley Ciarula|title=Dryden falls, Trudeau survives: Notable election winners and losers|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/federalbudget/article/984605--dryden-falls-trudeau-survives-notable-election-winners-and-losers?bn=1|access-date=2011-05-03|newspaper=[[Toronto Star]]|date=2011-05-03|archive-date=2011-05-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110506040353/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/federalbudget/article/984605--dryden-falls-trudeau-survives-notable-election-winners-and-losers?bn=1|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Recounts===
[[Elections Canada]] ordered three [[Judiciary|judicial]] [[election recount|recounts]],<ref name=GazetteRecount>{{cite news |last=Chai |first=Carmen |title=Elections Canada now reviewing 3 riding wins |url=https://montrealgazette.com/news/canada/Elections+Canada+reviewing+riding+wins/4735165/story.html |access-date=2011-05-05 |newspaper=[[Montreal Gazette]] |date=2011-05-05 |archive-date=2015-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150112140031/http://www.montrealgazette.com/news/canada/Elections+Canada+reviewing+riding+wins/4735165/story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> and an elector initiated a fourth.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/vote-recount-set-for-winnipeg-federal-riding-1.1110579 |title=Vote recount set for Winnipeg federal riding |publisher=[[CBC News]] |date=2011-05-13 |access-date=2011-05-14 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516065337/http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/story/2011/05/13/mb-recount-election-winnipeg.html |archive-date=2011-05-16}}</ref> The [[Canada Elections Act]] states that "a judicial recount is required when the difference in votes between the first- and second-place candidates is less than one one-thousandth of the total votes cast in a riding," and allows an elector or candidate in any riding to approach a judge and request a recount regardless of the final result.<ref name=GazetteRecount/> In all four ridings, [[Etobicoke Centre (federal electoral district)|Etobicoke Centre]], [[Montmagny—L'Islet—Kamouraska—Rivière-du-Loup]], [[Nipissing—Timiskaming]], and [[Winnipeg North]], the validated result was confirmed:
* As initially validated by election officials, [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] candidate [[Ted Opitz]] defeated Liberal incumbent [[Borys Wrzesnewskyj]] in [[Etobicoke Centre (federal electoral district)|Etobicoke Centre]] by 25 votes,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/crime/article/985959--judicial-recount-ordered-for-etobicoke-centre-riding |title=Judicial recount ordered for Etobicoke Centre riding |date=2011-05-04 |access-date=2011-05-04 |work=Toronto Star |first=Henry |last=Stancu |archive-date=2012-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024032213/http://www.thestar.com/news/crime/article/985959--judicial-recount-ordered-for-etobicoke-centre-riding |url-status=live}}</ref> a margin increased by one in the recount.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/conservative-opitz-wins-etobicoke-centre-recount-1.1067694 |title=Conservative Opitz wins Etobicoke Centre recount |work=CBC News |date=2011-05-23 |access-date=2011-05-23 |archive-date=2011-05-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525050055/http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/story/2011/05/23/ted-opitz-recount-etobicoke-centre.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Citing potential voter registration irregularities, however, Wrzesnewskyj has sought to have the result overturned by the courts, filing a formal motion with the [[Ontario Superior Court]] in spring 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=Etobicoke Centre election result marred by 'irregularities' |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/etobicoke-centre-election-result-marred-by-irregularities-1.1129422 |access-date=2021-05-03 |work=[[CBC News]] |date=2012-04-23 |archive-date=2016-09-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910104109/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/etobicoke-centre-election-result-marred-by-irregularities-1.1129422 |url-status=live}}</ref> On October 25, 2012, the [[Supreme Court of Canada]] upheld Opitz's narrow victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Judgements of the Supreme Court of Canada: Opitz v. Wrzesnewskyj|date=2012-10-25|url=http://scc.lexum.org/decisia-scc-csc/scc-csc/scc-csc/en/item/12635/index.do|archive-date=2012-10-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121027212853/http://scc.lexum.org/decisia-scc-csc/scc-csc/scc-csc/en/item/12635/index.do|url-status=live}}</ref>
* Initially, Conservative [[Jay Aspin]] defeated incumbent [[Anthony Rota]] of the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] by 15 votes in Nipissing—Timiskaming; the recount added three votes to the margin of victory.<ref name="WinnNipTim">{{cite news |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/recounts-confirm-liberal-victory-in-winnipeg-tory-win-in-northern-ontario/article2024876/ |title=Recounts confirm Liberal victory in Winnipeg, Tory win in Northern Ontario |work=The Globe and Mail |location=Canada |date=2011-05-17 |access-date=2011-05-17 |first=Gloria |last=Galloway |archive-date=2011-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111102052318/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/ottawa-notebook/recounts-confirm-liberal-victory-in-winnipeg-tory-win-in-northern-ontario/article2024876/ |url-status=live}}</ref>
* In Montmagny—L'Islet—Kamouraska—Rivière-du-Loup, incumbent Conservative MP [[Bernard Généreux]] was initially declared re-elected, but due to a counting error on election night, the seat was later determined to have been won by the NDP candidate [[François Lapointe (politician)|François Lapointe]] by a margin of five votes.<ref name=GazetteRecount/> The recount confirmed Lapointe as the winner by nine votes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/Recount+gives+59th+seat+Quebec/4785274/story.html |title=Recount gives NDP 59th seat in Quebec |work=[[Vancouver Sun]] |location=Canada |date=2011-05-14 |access-date=2011-05-15 |archive-date=2011-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517001619/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/decision-canada/Recount+gives+59th+seat+Quebec/4785274/story.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In Winnipeg North, a recount was requested by an elector; the difference between Liberal [[Kevin Lamoureux]], the victor, and New Democrat [[Rebecca Blaikie]] was just 45 votes,<ref name=CPWpg-North>{{cite news |title=Too close to be sure: judicial recount in Winnipeg North |url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/canadianpress/article/ALeqM5hlx9fkfvVDvIgGQva78aaVRr5Zkw?docId=6841615 |access-date=2011-05-13 |newspaper=[[Canadian Press]]}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> reduced by one vote in the recount.<ref name="WinnNipTim"/>

===Opposition party leadership changes===
Ignatieff announced on May 3, 2011, that he would step down as leader of the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] when it chose his successor.<ref name="StarResultsPostElection"/><ref name=NatPostLiblearesign>{{Cite news |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/ignatieff-press-conference-fuels-speculation-about-leaders-future |title=Ignatieff steps down as Liberal leader |work=[[National Post]] |location=Canada |date=2011-05-03 |access-date=2011-05-03 |archive-date=2021-08-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185725/https://nationalpost.com/category/news/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Ignatieff took a teaching position at the [[University of Toronto]] after his defeat in [[Etobicoke—Lakeshore (federal electoral district)|Etobicoke—Lakeshore]]. He decided to teach classes in the law faculty, the department of political science, the [[Munk School of Global Affairs]] and the School of Public Policy and Governance. Ignatieff stated that, "The life that I like the best is teaching. It's the end of my life as a politician".<ref name="Globeteaching">{{cite news|last=Valpy|first=Michael|title=Ignatieff says U of T teaching position to mark 'end of my life as a politician'|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/u-of-t-teaching-position-to-mark-the-end-of-my-life-as-a-politician/article2011390/|access-date=2011-05-05|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=2011-05-05|archive-date=2011-05-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110509051935/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/u-of-t-teaching-position-to-mark-the-end-of-my-life-as-a-politician/article2011390/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Bob Rae]], Liberal MP for [[Toronto Centre (federal electoral district)|Toronto Centre]] and former Premier of Ontario (1990 to 1995, as a New Democrat), subsequently became [[Interim leader (Canada)|interim leader]] of the Liberal Party, with a [[2013 Liberal Party of Canada leadership election|Liberal leadership election]] which took place April 14, 2013, during which Justin Trudeau was chosen as leader.

Duceppe resigned as Bloc Québécois leader on election night following his defeat.<ref name=StarResultsPostElection/> [[Louis Plamondon]], MP for [[Bas-Richelieu—Nicolet—Bécancour]] and [[Dean of the House (Canada)|Dean of the House]], subsequently became interim [[parliamentary leader]] of the Bloc. Former MP [[Daniel Paillé]], who lost his seat in the election, won the [[2011 Bloc Québécois leadership election|Bloc leadership election]] to succeed Duceppe on December 11, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/daniel-paill%C3%A9-new-leader-of-bloc-qu%C3%A9b%C3%A9cois-1.1073544|title=Daniel Paille new leader of Bloc Quebecois|work=[[CBC News]]|date=2011-12-11}}</ref>

On July 25, 2011, Jack Layton took a leave of absence to fight a newly diagnosed cancer. [[Nycole Turmel]], former union leader and newly elected MP for [[Hull—Aylmer]], was named interim leader of the New Democratic Party. On August 22, [[Death and state funeral of Jack Layton|Layton died]]. Turmel became opposition leader. A [[2012 New Democratic Party leadership election|leadership election]] was held on March 24, 2012, and [[Tom Mulcair]] was elected leader of the [[New Democratic Party (Canada)|New Democratic Party]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/mulcair-victorious-on-fourth-ballot/article2380309/|title=Mulcair victorious on fourth ballot|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209221439/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/mulcair-victorious-on-fourth-ballot/article2380309/ |archive-date=2017-02-09|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=2012-03-24}}</ref>

===Controversies===
The losing parties in the [[Berthier—Maskinongé]] riding claimed that the nomination papers for [[Ruth Ellen Brosseau]], the newly elected NDP Member of Parliament for the riding, had irregularities.<ref name=BrosseauIrregularities>{{cite news|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/985610--liberals-seek-revenge-on-quebec-mp-who-won-without-campaigning?bn=1|title=Liberals seek revenge on Quebec MP who won without campaigning|date=2011-05-04|first=Allan|last=Woods|access-date=2011-05-05|work=Toronto Star|archive-date=2011-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110508024417/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/985610--liberals-seek-revenge-on-quebec-mp-who-won-without-campaigning?bn=1|url-status=live}}</ref> Some of the alleged irregularities include writing an address instead of signing, missing signatures, people thinking they were signing a petition for the NDP to name a candidate in the riding and one person not remembering that he signed her nomination papers even though he admitted that the signature looks like his.<ref name=BrosseauIrregularities/> The NDP denied the allegations.<ref name=BrosseauIrregularities/> Elections Canada has insisted that Brosseau's nomination papers were legitimate.<ref name="SunBrosseauCleared">{{cite news|last=Minsky|first=Amy|title=New MP Ruth Ellen Brosseau cleared by Elections Canada|url=https://vancouversun.com/news/canada/Ruth+Ellen+Brosseau+cleared+Elections+Canada/4740008/story.html|access-date=2011-05-06|newspaper=[[Vancouver Sun]]|date=2011-05-06|archive-date=2016-06-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629104432/http://www.vancouversun.com/news/canada/Ruth+Ellen+Brosseau+cleared+Elections+Canada/4740008/story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Elections Canada stated that "The decision to overturn or uphold the results is at the discretion of the courts and not Elections Canada".<ref name="SunBrosseauCleared"/>

The [[Liberal Party of Canada]] attracted controversy regarding the past racist comments and White supremacist history of one of its candidates in northern Quebec, Andre Forbes. His history as a white supremacist activist and past hate speech against Muslims, First Nations and LGBTQ+ people was uncovered by the NDP.  Liberal leader Michael Ignatieff immediately removed Forbes as a candidate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://metronews.ca/news/202277/claims-of-racism-against-liberal-candidate-dog-ignatieff-in-quebec/|title=Claims of racism against Liberal candidate dog Ignatieff in Quebec|work=Metro|access-date=2015-02-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203100031/http://metronews.ca/news/202277/claims-of-racism-against-liberal-candidate-dog-ignatieff-in-quebec/|archive-date=2015-02-03|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Voter suppression scandal====

{{main|2011 Canadian federal election voter suppression scandal}}

In early 2012, there were allegations of voter suppression during the election, starting the [[robocall scandal]]. [[Elections Canada]] and the [[Royal Canadian Mounted Police]] (RCMP) investigated claims that robocalls were used in an attempt to dissuade voters from casting their ballot by telling them their poll stations had changed location.<ref name="MaherFeb27">{{cite news|url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/Elections+Canada+investigating+robocalls+that+misled+voters/6194990/story.html |title=Elections Canada investigating 'robocalls' that misled voters |access-date=2012-03-18 |last=Maher |first=Stephen |last2=McGregor |first2=Glen |date=2012-02-27 |work=[[Ottawa Citizen]]}}{{dead link|date=November 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> While the Elections Canada investigation initially focused on calls sent into Guelph amidst nationwide complaints, the investigation continued to expand in scope and to examine complaints in other ridings across the country. Reports of fraudulent automated or live calls targeting opposition supporters were published in 100 ridings<ref>{{cite web |first=David P. |last=Ball |url=http://www.vancouverobserver.com/world/canada/2012/02/27/robogate-election-scandal-11-robo-call-ridings-linked-conservatives-11-seat |title=Robocall scandal by the numbers: up to 100 ridings allege election fraud |publisher=The Vancouver Observer |date=2012-02-29 |access-date=2012-03-27 |archive-date=2012-04-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120411135912/http://www.vancouverobserver.com/world/canada/2012/02/27/robogate-election-scandal-11-robo-call-ridings-linked-conservatives-11-seat |url-status=live}}</ref> and Elections Canada acknowledged it was investigating telephone election fraud complaints in 247 of Canada's 308 federal ridings.

On March 27, 2012, the [[Council of Canadians]] announced that they had launched a lawsuit in the [[Federal Court of Canada]] to ask for by-elections to be ordered in seven ridings where complaints were received and where Conservatives had won by slim margins. The ridings named were Don Valley East, Winnipeg South Centre, Saskatoon-Rosetown-Biggar, Vancouver Island North, Yukon, Nipissing-Timiskaming and Elmwood-Transcona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vancouversun.com/business/fp/yourmoney/Tories+offensive+over+robocalls/6234917/story.html |title=Tories go on offensive over robocalls |publisher=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=2012-03-02 |access-date=2012-03-26 |archive-date=2012-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305034226/http://www.vancouversun.com/business/fp/yourmoney/Tories+offensive+over+robocalls/6234917/story.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Maher27Mar12">{{cite news|url = https://ottawacitizen.com/news/Robocalls+Activist+group+files+legal+challenge+results+seven+ridings/6362995/story.html|title = Robocalls: Activist group files legal challenge of results in seven ridings|access-date=2012-03-27|last1 = Maher|first1 = Stephen |last2 = McGregor |first2 = Glen|date=2012-03-27|work = [[Ottawa Citizen]]|archive-date=2012-03-28|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120328160241/http://www.ottawacitizen.com/news/Robocalls+Activist+group+files+legal+challenge+results+seven+ridings/6362995/story.html|url-status = live}}</ref> The case was heard over two weeks starting December 9, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Campion-Smith |first1=Bruce |last2=Wittington |first2=Les|title=Elections Canada reveals massive robo-calls probe of 2011 election|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/1296114--elections-canada-reveals-massive-robo-calls-probe-of-2011-election|access-date=2012-12-12|newspaper=[[Toronto Star]]|date=2012-11-30|archive-date=2012-12-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121204112808/http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/politics/article/1296114--elections-canada-reveals-massive-robo-calls-probe-of-2011-election|url-status=live}}</ref> Justice Richard G. Mosley ruled in May 2013 that fraud had occurred in Guelph and that voting irregularities and misconduct occurred in all six of the contested ridings, but that it was not significant enough to warrant overturning the election results. The judge also ruled that the mostly likely source of the fraud was the Conservative Party of Canada's (using the CIMS database) and that there was no evidence that its use was approved by the CPC.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wingrove|first=Josh|date=2013-05-23|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/federal-ruling-dismisses-robo-call-appeal-clears-tories/article12121319/|title=Robo-calls had minimal impact on 2011 election, court rules, upholding results|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209221233/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/federal-ruling-dismisses-robo-call-appeal-clears-tories/article12121319/ |archive-date=2017-02-09|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]]|access-date=2013-05-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/federal-court-won-t-remove-mps-over-election-robocalls-1.1331781 |title=Federal Court won't remove MPs over robocall allegations – Politics – CBC News |publisher=[[CBC News]] |date=2013-05-23 |access-date=2013-05-24 |archive-date=2013-05-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524025949/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/story/2013/05/23/pol-federal-court-robocall-allegations.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2013, a criminal charge in the matter was laid on [[Michael Sona]], a former Conservative staffer who was the communications officer and official Ottawa liaison for the Guelph Conservative campaign.<ref>{{cite news|title=Guelph Conservatives felt national party influence, documents suggest|url=http://www.guelphmercury.com/news/local/article/680217--guelph-conservatives-felt-national-party-influence-documents-suggest|newspaper=Guelph Mercury|access-date=2013-04-12|archive-date=2021-08-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185725/https://www.guelphmercury.com/guelph-on-news/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=More robocall suspects likely, Guelph MP says|url=http://www.guelphmercury.com/news/local/article/912853--more-robocall-suspects-likely-guelph-mp-says|newspaper=Guelph Mercury|access-date=2013-04-12|archive-date=2021-08-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807185750/https://www.guelphmercury.com/guelph-on-news/|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2014, he was convicted of the charge.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/michael-sona-guilty-in-robocalls-trial-1.2735676|title=Michael Sona guilty in robocalls trial – but 'did not likely act alone'|newspaper=CBC|access-date=2014-08-15|archive-date=2014-08-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814183953/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/michael-sona-guilty-in-robocalls-trial-1.2735676|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Riding of Vaughan====

In a further scandal, Elections Canada was called on to investigate the finances of [[Associate Minister of National Defence (Canada)|Associate Minister of National Defence]] [[Julian Fantino]]'s election finances after three former Conservative riding executives from [[Vaughan (federal electoral district)|Vaughan]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://404systemerror.com/election-fraud-robocalls-the-case-of-vaughan/ |title=Election Fraud & Robocalls: The Case of Vaughan |publisher=404 System Error |date=2012-03-08 |access-date=2012-03-26 |archive-date=2012-03-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312154457/http://404systemerror.com/election-fraud-robocalls-the-case-of-vaughan/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canada.com/news/Three+former+Tory+association+members+seek+probe+into+Fantino+election+finances/6280438/story.html |title=Three former Tory association members seek probe into Fantino's election finances |publisher=Canada.com |date=2012-03-09 |access-date=2012-03-26}}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> signed affidavits alleging impropriety in Fantino's 2010 and 2011 election campaigns. They alleged there was a second, secret, illegal bank account containing $300,000.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ex-tory-riding-execs-question-fantino-s-election-finances-1.1147707 |title=Ex-Tory riding execs question Fantino's election finances|publisher=[[CBC News]] |date=2012-03-09 |access-date=2012-03-26 |archive-date=2012-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313011311/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/story/2012/03/09/pol-fantino-election.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Commentary ===
In the wake of the election, pundits widely believed in a theme of major [[political realignment]].<ref>Royce Koop, and Amanda Bittner, "Parties and Elections after 2011: The Fifth Canadian Party System?." in Amanda Bittner and Royce Koop, eds, ''Parties, Elections, and the Future of Canadian Politics'' (2013): 308-31.</ref> The ''Economist'' said, "the election represents the biggest realignment of Canadian politics since [[1993 Canadian federal election|1993]]."<ref>''Economist'' May 3, 2011</ref> [[Lawrence Martin (journalist)|Lawrence Martin]], commentator for ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', claimed that "Harper has completed a remarkable reconstruction of a Canadian political landscape that endured for more than a century. The realignment sees both old parties of the moderate middle, the Progressive Conservatives and the Liberals, either eliminated or marginalized."<ref>{{cite news |last=Martin |first=Lawrence |date=2011-05-04 |title=Harper's triumph: a realignment of historic proportion |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/opinions/opinion/harpers-triumph-a-realignment-of-historic-proportions/article2008719/ |access-date=2011-11-09 |archive-date=2011-12-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111216043610/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/opinions/opinion/harpers-triumph-a-realignment-of-historic-proportions/article2008719/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Maclean's]]'', [[Andrew Coyne]] proclaimed "The West is in and Ontario has joined it," observing that the Conservatives achieved their majority predominantly due to strength in both Ontario and the western provinces (an electoral combination that was historically unlikely due to the low population of the latter); this, he argued, marked "the new axis of Canadian politics", and that "the Conservatives are now in a position to replace the Liberals as the [[natural governing party]] in Canada."<!--<ref>{{cite news |last = Stinson |first = Scott |title = Redefining the Liberals not a quick process |url = https://nationalpost.com/full-comment/scott-stinson-liberals-begin-process-of-redefinition |access-date = 2011-11-09 |newspaper = National Post |date = 2011-05-06}}</ref>--><ref>{{cite news |last=Coyne |first=Andrew |date=2011-05-06 |title=The West is in and Ontario has joined it |newspaper=Maclean's |url=http://www.macleans.ca/general/a-new-power-couple/ |access-date=2011-11-09 |archive-date=2014-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905192804/http://www.macleans.ca/general/a-new-power-couple/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Books such as ''The Big Shift'' by [[John Ibbitson]] and [[Darrell Bricker]], and [[Peter C. Newman]]'s ''When the Gods Changed: The Death of Liberal Canada'',  provocatively asserted that the Liberals had become an "endangered species" and that an NDP-led opposition would mean that "fortune favours the Harper government" in subsequent campaigns.<ref>{{cite news |last=McLeod |first=Paul |date=2015-10-22 |title=Book Review: The Big Shift Explains Why Stephen Harper Will Keep Winning |publisher=Buzzfeed |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/paulmcleod/book-review-the-big-shift-why-stephen-harper-will-keep-winni#.kk8WgyWkW |access-date=2015-10-22 |archive-date=2015-10-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023222156/http://www.buzzfeed.com/paulmcleod/book-review-the-big-shift-why-stephen-harper-will-keep-winni#.kk8WgyWkW |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Valpy |first=Michael |date=2011-11-25 |title=Is a Liberal comeback mission impossible? |newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]] |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/is-a-liberal-comeback-mission-impossible/article4246976/ |access-date=2015-10-22 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304223625/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/is-a-liberal-comeback-mission-impossible/article4246976/ |url-status=live}}</ref> However, the resurgence of the Liberal Party in the [[2015 Canadian federal election|2015 election]] has since challenged that narrative.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nadelli |first1=Alberto |last2=Swann |first2=Glenn |date=2015-10-20 |title=Three maps that explain the Liberals' great comeback in Canada's election |newspaper=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/datablog/2015/oct/20/canada-election-liberal-comeback-three-maps-justin-trudeau |access-date=2015-10-21 |archive-date=2015-10-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021134027/http://www.theguardian.com/news/datablog/2015/oct/20/canada-election-liberal-comeback-three-maps-justin-trudeau |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Paikin |first=Steve |date=2015-10-19 |title=Who says Canadian politics are boring? |publisher=TVO |url=http://tvo.org/blog/current-affairs/who-says-canadian-politics-are-boring |access-date=2011-10-21 |archive-date=2015-12-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222114454/http://tvo.org/blog/current-affairs/who-says-canadian-politics-are-boring |url-status=live}}</ref>
== Student vote results ==
Student votes are [[mock election]]s that run parallel to actual elections, in which students not of [[voting age]] participate. They are administered by Student Vote Canada. Student vote elections are for educational purposes and do not count towards the results. Though there were 308 ridings, only 301 were declared.<ref name="studentvote">{{cite web |url=https://studentvote.ca/federal2015/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/FED-SEC-EN-Handout-4.4.pdf |title=2011 Election Results |publisher=Student Vote Canada |access-date=2025-05-05}}</ref>
